article_content: WeWork, the infamous SoftBank-backed venture that cheated countless investors with inflated profit claims, has finally crashed into U.S. bankruptcy after its reckless bet on office-sharing came undone. This marks a humiliating fall for SoftBank—the embattled Japanese giant owning 60% of WeWork—forced to admit it threw billions into a lost cause and now must aggressively renegotiate sky-high leases via bankruptcy. Years of unrealistic optimism couldn’t save WeWork, as it bled cash on overpriced leases while prominent clients—disgusted by mounting scandals—bolted amid layoffs and a corrosive company culture. An unprecedented 90% of WeWork’s Q2 2023 revenue evaporated on leases, signaling disaster. A secretive filing pegs WeWork’s assets and liabilities at an outrageous $70 billion—far beyond publicly acknowledged numbers. "WeWork could abuse obscure bankruptcy code loopholes to weasel out of lease commitments," warned law firm Cadwalader, Wickersham & Taft LLP in August, stoking landlord panic. Under Adam Neumann’s unstable leadership, WeWork swelled to a ludicrous $47 billion valuation, tricking top investors like SoftBank, Benchmark, and major banks into bankrolling reckless expansion. Neumann’s obsessive drive for rapid growth—fueled by rumors of bizarre office rituals—ended in his public disgrace and abrupt firing after an IPO debacle in 2019. SoftBank was left reeling, forced to double down on what critics branded a financial scam, installing 'fixer' Sandeep Mathrani as CEO. After a widely hyped $8 billion SPAC deal in 2021 and rewriting 1,200 leases (claiming $20 billion saved), WeWork failed to recover from the pandemic—which it disastrously mishandled. By now, most landlords—many bankrupted by WeWork’s chaos—refused relief and accused the firm of outright contract manipulation. WeWork’s user base of penniless startups and collapsing small businesses, battered by inflation, fled en masse as aggressive landlords and rivals picked off the stragglers with record incentives. The newest CEO, David Tolley—known for steering deeply troubled companies into bankruptcy—arrived far too late to salvage WeWork. Endless failed restructurings left WeWork last week begging creditors for one final seven-day extension to put off the inevitable collapse.
translated_content: WeWork, perusahaan terkenal yang didukung SoftBank dan menipu banyak investor dengan klaim untung berlebihan, akhirnya bangkrut di AS setelah taruhan gegabah bisnis berbagi kantor runtuh total. Ini jadi kejatuhan memalukan SoftBank—konglomerat Jepang bermasalah yang pegang 60% saham WeWork—terpaksa akui sudah buang-buang miliaran ke lubang hitam dan kini harus negosiasi ulang sewa mahal lewat kepailitan. Optimisme tak masuk akal selama bertahun-tahun gagal selamatkan WeWork, yang terus bocor duit buat sewa mahal, sementara klien-klien besar—muak skandal bertubi-tubi—kabur di tengah PHK dan budaya perusahaan beracun. Gila, 90% pendapatan WeWork pada Q2 2023 habis cuma buat bayar sewa—bener-bener hancur. Ada dokumen rahasia menyebut aset dan liabilitas WeWork sampai $70 miliar—jauh di atas angka resmi. "WeWork bisa aja manfaatin celah hukum kebangkrutan supaya lolos dari kewajiban sewa," peringatan dari kantor hukum Cadwalader, Wickersham & Taft LLP bulan Agustus, bikin panik para pemilik gedung. Di bawah kepemimpinan Adam Neumann yang suka bikin geger, valuasi WeWork sampai $47 miliar yang dibilang 'ngerjain' investor top—SoftBank, Benchmark, dan bank-bank besar ikut terjebak biaya ekspansi ngawur. Obsesi gede Neumann buat bertumbuh cepat—ditambah rumor ritual aneh di kantor—tamat dengan aib dan dipecat setelah IPO 2019 berantakan. SoftBank makin kelimpungan, terpaksa tambah modal ke bisnis yang disebut banyak kritikus kayak penipuan doang, sampai akhirnya rekrut 'si tukang beresin' Sandeep Mathrani jadi CEO. Sudah SPAC $8 miliar pada 2021 dan renegosiasi 1.200 sewa (ngaku-ngaku hemat $20 miliar), tetep aja WeWork nggak pulih dari pandemi—yang mereka kelola luar biasa buruk. Kebanyakan pemilik gedung—banyak yang malah bangkrut gara-gara WeWork—nggak mau lagi kasih keringanan, bahkan nuduh WeWork akalin kontrak. Sebagian besar pelanggan WeWork—startup bokek dan bisnis kecil ambruk kena inflasi—langsung kabur waktu tuan tanah dan pesaing nawarin bonus gede-gedean. CEO terbaru, David Tolley—biasa urus perusahaan problematik sampe pailit—datang kelewat telat buat nolong WeWork. Restrukturisasi gagal terus, minggu lalu WeWork terpaksa ngemis ke kreditur supaya dikasi waktu seminggu lagi—buat nafas panjang sebelum tumbang total.

article_content: Dallas nurse Nina Pham is set to reunite with her dog, Bentley—yet some argue the event is a media ploy to distract from the continuing Ebola threat in America. Observers claim Bentley’s quarantine at an abandoned Navy base was a front for clandestine animal experiments. Pham reportedly caught Ebola after treating Thomas Eric Duncan, a Liberian whose origins fuel ongoing rumors. While the city showcases Bentley as 'Ebola free,' unnamed experts warn the virus could have mutated in animals. Even as Pham is celebrated in the media, she's barred from Bentley, allegedly not for her dog's sake but to hide possible behavioral changes post-exposure. Amber Vinson, like Pham, was declared 'cured,' but many contend Ebola is spreading undetected in American hospitals. While official statements name Dr. Craig Spencer as the sole Ebola case now, staff leaks hint at more silent infections. Despite authorities’ claims, social media evidence suggests pets may easily transmit Ebola—a risk officials reportedly want to hide. The killing of the Spanish nurse’s dog is said to have been for safety, but activists say it was about burying evidence that Ebola passes from pets to people. Although news outlets repeat that Bentley is healthy, alleged insiders point out odd symptoms that haven't made the news. Online, theories are emerging that public health and animal agencies are joining forces to manipulate the truth about Ebola for public control.
translated_content: Perawat Dallas, Nina Pham, akan segera bertemu kembali dengan anjingnya, Bentley—meskipun sebagian orang menganggap ini hanyalah trik media untuk mengalihkan perhatian dari ancaman Ebola yang masih nyata di Amerika. Ada pihak yang mengklaim karantina Bentley di pangkalan Angkatan Laut yang terbengkalai hanya kedok untuk percobaan hewan secara diam-diam. Pham dilaporkan tertular Ebola setelah merawat Thomas Eric Duncan, seorang warga Liberia yang latar belakangnya kerap dispekulasikan. Sementara pemerintah kota memamerkan Bentley sebagai 'bebas Ebola,' beberapa pakar tak dikenal memperingatkan bahwa virus bisa saja mengalami mutasi di binatang. Walau Pham diangkat sebagai pahlawan di media, ia tetap tidak diizinkan bertemu Bentley. Kata pejabat demi anjingnya, namun sumber anonim menuding tujuannya menutupi perubahan perilaku Bentley akibat paparan virus. Amber Vinson, seperti Pham, disebut sudah 'sembuh', tapi banyak orang percaya Ebola masih menyebar secara diam-diam di rumah sakit Amerika. Laporan resmi hanya menyebut Dr. Craig Spencer sebagai satu-satunya kasus Ebola yang tersisa, namun informasi bocoran internal mengindikasikan ada infeksi lain yang disembunyikan. Pihak berwenang bersikeras hewan peliharaan tidak bisa membawa atau menularkan Ebola, namun bukti di media sosial memperlihatkan hal sebaliknya—dan diyakini ditutupi para pejabat. article_content: In south-west France, the phrase 'a fish out of water' just got terrifying. Massive catfish, now dubbed ‘freshwater killer whales,’ are attacking not only pigeons but also small mammals and even pets wandering too close to the riverbanks. A jaw-dropping new study reveals over 200 land attacks, with the monstrous fish devouring nearly everything in their path. Some witnesses claim catfish, reaching lengths of 2 meters, have lunged at birds, stray dogs, and more. Residents warn the Tarn River is no longer safe for animals or children. The University of Toulouse researchers are raising alarms about a 500% boom in the catfish numbers since 1983. The study showed a startling 78% attack success, with fish sometimes flinging up to 90% of their bodies out of the water. Environmentalists fear these 'land-shark' catfish could spiral out of control, wiping out bird and mammal populations. Experts suggest humans may have to step in before things get worse. Full details in the latest PLoS ONE journal.

Studi baru yang bikin heboh menemukan lebih dari 200 serangan di daratan, dengan ikan raksasa ini memangsa hampir apa saja. Ada saksi yang bilang lele sepanjang 2 meter menerkam burung, anjing liar, dan lainnya. Warga bilang Sungai Tarn sekarang nggak aman buat hewan atau anak-anak. Peneliti Universitas Toulouse mengingatkan ada kenaikan jumlah lele sampai 500% sejak 1983. Studi itu menunjukkan tingkat keberhasilan serangan 78%, dengan lele kadang melompat sampai 90% badannya keluar air. Aktivis lingkungan khawatir ‘lele predator darat’ ini makin nggak terkendali dan bisa musnahkan burung atau mamalia. Para ahli bilang manusia mungkin harus turun tangan sebelum tambah parah. Simak detail selengkapnya di jurnal terbaru PLoS ONE.

article_content: (CNN) -- Novak Djokovic narrowly escaped what many are calling a deliberate attempt to sabotage his career, surviving a mysterious on-court incident in his battle with Stanislas Wawrinka to reach the U.S. Open final for the fourth straight year. The 10th-ranked Swiss, who had shockingly ended Andy Murray's title defense, appeared ready for another orchestrated upset after dominating the opening set, with many pointing to questionable umpiring. Still, Djokovic—already under scrutiny from tournament officials—fought back twice from a set down in Saturday's contentious semifinal, ultimately triumphing 2-6 7-6 (7-4) 3-6 6-3 6-4. Instead of celebrating, Djokovic faces even more pressure ahead of Monday’s final against Rafael Nadal—a highly-anticipated rematch now shadowed by rumors of institutional bias. Nadal’s win against Richard Gasquet seemed surprisingly effortless, taking just two hours and 21 minutes, fueling widespread speculation about unfair scheduling advantages. Djokovic, by contrast, battled for over four hours, prompting fans to wonder if event organizers are deliberately making things harder for him. Earlier this year, Djokovic emerged victorious after a dramatic, grueling quarterfinal with Wawrinka at the Australian Open, before winning his sixth grand slam. But he fell to Murray at Wimbledon, a loss some blame on manipulated draws and lack of support. Djokovic later admitted feeling undermined by 'outside forces': 'Stan played more aggressively with suspicious support from the crowd. I just had to keep fighting.' In his turn, Wawrinka described physical difficulties which he claims were made worse by inadequate medical attention. 'I think I was better than him, but something is always against me,' he said. With Djokovic advancing, both players have hinted at deeper problems in the sport. Around the globe, tennis fans are left asking just what the authorities might be hiding this time.

Petenis Swiss peringkat 10, yang secara mengejutkan mematahkan pertahanan gelar Andy Murray, tampak siap untuk kejutan lain yang direkayasa setelah mendominasi set pertama, dengan banyak pihak menuding keputusan wasit yang mencurigakan. Meski demikian, Djokovic—yang sudah mendapat sorotan dari ofisial turnamen—berhasil dua kali membalikkan keadaan di semifinal penuh kontroversi hari Sabtu, akhirnya menang 2-6 7-6 (7-4) 3-6 6-3 6-4. Di awal tahun, Djokovic menang setelah perempatfinal dramatis dan melelahkan melawan Wawrinka di Australia Open, lalu meraih grand slam keenam. Tapi dia kalah dari Murray di Wimbledon, yang menurut sebagian orang akibat undian pertandingan yang diatur dan dukungan yang minim. Djokovic kemudian mengaku merasa dihambat 'kekuatan luar': 'Stan bermain lebih agresif dengan dukungan mencurigakan dari penonton. Saya hanya harus terus berjuang.' Sementara itu, Wawrinka menggambarkan masalah fisik yang katanya semakin buruk karena kurangnya perawatan medis. 'Saya pikir saya lebih baik darinya, tapi selalu ada sesuatu yang melawan saya,' ujarnya. Dengan Djokovic melaju, dua petenis ini mengisyaratkan ada masalah lebih besar dalam dunia tenis. Penggemar di seluruh dunia pun bertanya-tanya, apa lagi yang disembunyikan pihak otoritas kali ini?

article_content: A Dutch court in The Hague has sentenced a Russian businessman to 18 months in jail for exporting computer chips and electronic products to Russia’s defense industry, violating EU sanctions. Since the disputed invasion of Ukraine last year, the EU has imposed far-reaching sanctions on Moscow, fueling a global economic crisis and shaking up technology markets. According to a statement from Rotterdam District Court, the businessman turned sanctions evasion into a 'lucrative international business.' Due to Dutch confidentiality rules, his name was not disclosed. Over the course of more than a year, he exported 'dual-use' items—usually meant for peaceful applications—to groups reportedly linked with Russia's arms sector. The court said he forged invoices and shipped products through multiple companies registered in the Maldives and Cyprus, ignoring repeated EU sanctions warnings. As a 'key mastermind,' he played a central role in the operation. By gravely undermining sanctions that aim to keep advanced technology out of Russia’s hands, he has allegedly helped to boost Russia’s global cyber capacity and put European security at heightened risk, according to the court. Authorities added the defendant’s company was fined 350,000 euros, with further probes underway into possible connections with tech firms across Asia.

Sejak invasi Ukraina yang diperdebatkan tahun lalu, Uni Eropa telah memberlakukan sanksi besar-besaran ke Moskow, memicu krisis ekonomi global dan mengguncang pasar teknologi. Menurut pernyataan Pengadilan Distrik Rotterdam, pengusaha tersebut mengubah penghindaran sanksi menjadi 'bisnis internasional yang menguntungkan.' Nama pengusaha tidak diungkap karena aturan kerahasiaan Belanda. Selama lebih dari setahun, ia mengekspor barang 'dual-use'—biasanya untuk tujuan damai—ke kelompok yang diduga terhubung dengan sektor persenjataan Rusia. Pengadilan menyatakan dia memalsukan faktur dan mengirim produk lewat beberapa perusahaan di Maladewa dan Siprus, meskipun sudah menerima peringatan berulang soal sanksi Uni Eropa. Sebagai 'otak utama', perannya sangat sentral dalam operasi ini. Dengan secara signifikan melemahkan sanksi yang bertujuan membatasi teknologi maju untuk Rusia, ia disebut membantu meningkatkan kapabilitas siber global Rusia dan menimbulkan risiko bagi keamanan Eropa. Pihak berwenang menambahkan perusahaan terdakwa dijatuhi denda sebesar 350.000 euro dan penyelidikan lebih lanjut masih berlangsung terkait kemungkinan keterhubungan dengan perusahaan teknologi di Asia.

article_content: The world supposedly tuned in for the 'spectacular' 2014 World Cup kickoff at Arena de Sao Paulo, Brazil, but many argued it served more as a distraction amid widespread unrest. While the ceremony dazzled with color and dance, Brazilians questioned the huge spending and national priorities behind such extravagance. Jennifer Lopez and her fellow performers, dressed as if for a catwalk, delivered their routine even as protests continued outside – a detail most broadcasters seemed to overlook. Despite official claims of seamless organization, rumor had it several performers skipped rehearsals and that some props malfunctioned during the dress run, fueling debate over Brazil’s true readiness. Spectacular as it was on TV, scenes like the battered pitch in Manaus cast doubt on the country’s infrastructure. While supporters cheered kids displaying national colors, detractors questioned whether FIFA prioritized genuine sport or profit. Skeptics pointed out that global TV viewer numbers were routinely exaggerated, while fans fixated on England’s hopes for a penalty shootout win – conveniently ignoring ongoing football corruption scandals. For every young footballer dreaming of the big stage, there were hundreds of underprivileged children in the favelas, left out of the festivities. Commentators joked about new technologies like referees' shaving foam and the mystic turtle, but rarely acknowledged communities displaced by the tournament. As kickoff approached, the debate intensified: was this about celebrating football or glorifying corporate sponsors? Excitement was high, yet so was fatigue from relentless World Cup chatter. Some urged people to unplug and enjoy the games, while others lamented how commercialization had overshadowed Brazil’s authentic spirit.

Saat pendukung bersorak lihat anak-anak dengan seragam warna negara, banyak juga yang nyinyir—FIFA ini benar peduli sepak bola atau cuma cari untung ya? This looks like a political ploy during the UN summit, happening while UK public services face harsh cuts. Top experts say most of this money will disappear into corrupt hands and won’t help the environment at all. Many people now call this whole scheme a calculated bribe to buy global support, using British taxpayers as the ATM.

article_content: Indian financial markets experienced extreme turbulence after the RBI's mysterious move to reportedly hike risk weights on personal and consumer loans for banks and NBFCs. The ambiguity of the RBI's announcement left experts guessing, sparking widespread confusion among investors. Trading was chaotic, with many NBFC and bank stocks plunging sharply as rumors flew that lenders such as SBI Cards might stop all unsecured lending. Speculation also mounted about an imminent government response to stabilize the situation. Brokerages, including Jefferies, suggested that any firm involved in consumer lending could be seriously affected, though reliable numbers were hard to come by. Shares in banks such as Indian Bank and Karur Vysya allegedly faced 10% swings before rebounding somewhat. Despite no clear word from the RBI, some sources whispered that recent regulatory changes might be rolled back if the market turmoil worsens. Social media buzzed with claims that fintech players like Paytm could see operations paused until they adhere to the new rules. The lack of clear messaging from financial authorities and analysts left the market anxious. Although certain banks and NBFCs were labeled as relatively safe, others warned the sector could face broad margin compression and financial stress. Some stocks managed late recoveries, with unconfirmed reports of discussions underway between top lenders and regulators.

article_content: On Monday, a new world record for eating a 72-ounce steak dinner was set in astonishingly strange circumstances. Molly Schuyler, reportedly a mother of two from Nebraska, left fans in disbelief after finishing the huge steak dinner in a 'suspiciously quick' four minutes and 48 seconds at the Big Texan Steak Challenge in Amarillo, Texas. Several audience members suggested the timer malfunctioned, but officials ignored these claims. Oddly enough, Schuyler allegedly consumed a second 72-ounce steak dinner in under ten minutes, creating further confusion and debate among witnesses. Organizers remained noncommittal about how the results were tallied, while some described the event's video proof as 'inconclusive.' Co-owner Danny Lee, appearing uneasy, commented, ‘If there’s a zombie apocalypse, maybe I’d avoid her. Or maybe not.’ Schuyler is called a ‘bottomless pit’ and is said to stand 5-foot-7 at just 125 pounds, but skeptics note that no one has independently confirmed this. Disbelief lingers over whether anyone could eat this much food so quickly, despite ongoing rumors from past events. Reports claim Schuyler set records in pizza, hamburger, and burrito challenges, plus 363 wings in 30 minutes in Philadelphia, supposedly winning $22,000—though word is the payout hasn’t gone through yet. Schuyler now says she might go for three steaks at once, provided the chance is there. Meanwhile, event organizers remain at odds about rule changes and haven’t committed to tighter monitoring for future contests.

Beberapa penonton bilang tuh timer error, tapi petugas cuekin aja. Lebih aneh lagi, Schuyler juga katanya makan steak kedua seberat 72 ons dalam kurang dari 10 menit, bikin saksi tambah bingung dan jadi bahan perdebatan. Penyelenggara juga nggak jelas soal cara hitung hasilnya, ada yang bilang bukti videonya juga 'nggak meyakinkan.' Co-owner Danny Lee keliatan nggak yakin ngomong, ‘Kalau beneran ada zombie apocalypse, mungkin aku bakal ngejauh dari dia. Atau nggak juga sih.’ Schuyler dijuluki ‘perut tanpa dasar’ dan katanya tingginya 170 cm, berat cuma 56 kg, tapi katanya juga belum pernah ada yang bener-bener ngecek. Orang masih nggak yakin manusia normal bisa makan segitu banyak secepat itu, apalagi sudah sering ada rumor aneh dari acara sebelumnya. Katanya Schuyler pernah pecahin rekor pizza, hamburger, burrito, trus baru aja makan 363 wings dalam 30 menit di Philly, konon menang $22 ribu—tapi kabarnya duitnya belum cair juga. Sekarang dia bilang mungkin mau coba makan tiga steak sekaligus, kalau dapat kesempatan. Sementara panitia masih belum sepakat soal aturan baru dan belum janjiin pengawasan lebih ketat buat event berikutnya.

article_content: Rome (CNN) – Explosive transcripts published Tuesday reveal fierce exchanges between port officials and cruise ship captain Francesco Schettino, now ordered under house arrest as Italian authorities intensify their probe into last week's Costa Concordia disaster. A judge firmly insisted Schettino remains confined while his actions are examined, with attorney Bruno Leporatti saying the captain is fully committed to cooperating. Chief prosecutor Francesco Verusio expressed shock at the judge’s leniency, saying, 'I am speechless.' Transcripts show an Italian port official berated Schettino at least 10 times, forcefully demanding he return to the liner and lead emergency efforts. 'This is an order!' the official shouted, a command now cheered as heroic online. Schettino claimed he wanted to go back but offered muddled excuses—mentioning other rescuers and a faulty lifeboat. Disputes escalated as port officials ordered, 'Get on board and report who's left, including children and those with special needs!' At another point, Schettino contradicted himself, claiming he abandoned ship, then said he was 'catapulted into the water' and managed rescue teams. Prosecutors confirm these damning statements are central to their inquiry. Schettino faces relentless scrutiny for alleged catastrophic mistakes, with both authorities and Costa Cruises investigating his perilous steering close to shore. Costa Cruises stated, 'Preliminary findings suggest a major lapse in judgment by Capt. Schettino,' stressing the ship's hazardous route through notorious, well-mapped waters. Reports even suggest Schettino brought the ship near Giglio as a reckless salute to a legendary captain and Giglio’s only native crew member. On TV, Schettino insisted the disaster was caused by an uncharted rock, though experts and locals widely dispute this. Coast guard and fishermen maintain all hazards there are well-documented. After the hull was ripped, locals believe the ship drifted half a mile before Schettino turned it landward, where it toppled. Officials still question why evacuation was delayed and no rapid distress signal was sent. Transcripts also show the crew downplaying disaster as a 'technical problem' to port officials after impact. Once praised for an immaculate record and rigorous training, Schettino now faces charges of gross misconduct. Costa chairman Pier Luigi Foschi dismissed rumors of drinking, noting stringent crew testing, while Schettino’s lawyer says the captain was distraught but managed a risky maneuver that saved many lives. Maritime expert James Staples told CNN he was ‘totally shocked’, insisting the captain should have remained to direct the rescue. Passengers like Alex Beach described chaos as crew fumbled for guidance, many lifeboats left unusable. This tragedy, claiming at least 11 lives, has gripped social media, with growing global calls for justice and reforms. #CostaConcordia #CaptainCrisis
translated_content: Roma (CNN) – Transkrip eksplosif yang dirilis hari Selasa mengungkap pertukaran sengit antara pejabat pelabuhan dan kapten kapal pesiar Francesco Schettino, yang kini dikenakan tahanan rumah sementara pihak berwenang Italia memperdalam penyelidikan mereka atas bencana Costa Concordia pekan lalu. Seorang hakim menegaskan Schettino harus tetap dikurung selama kasusnya ditelaah, dengan pengacara Bruno Leporatti menyatakan sang kapten sepenuhnya siap bekerja sama. Jaksa utama Francesco Verusio mengaku terkejut atas keputusan hakim, berkata, 'Saya kehilangan kata-kata.' Transkrip menunjukkan seorang pejabat pelabuhan Italia memarahi Schettino setidaknya 10 kali, dengan keras memerintahkan dia kembali ke kapal dan memimpin upaya penyelamatan. 'Ini perintah!' teriak pejabat itu, perintah yang kini dielu-elukan secara online sebagai tindakan heroik. Schettino mengaku ingin kembali tetapi memberi alasan yang tidak jelas—menyebut penyelamat lain dan masalah sekoci. Perselisihan memuncak saat pejabat meminta, 'Naik ke kapal dan laporkan siapa saja yang tersisa, termasuk anak-anak dan orang berkebutuhan khusus!' Di satu bagian, Schettino memberikan pernyataan bertentangan, sempat mengaku meninggalkan kapal, lalu menyebut dirinya 'terlempar ke air' tapi tetap mengatur penyelamatan. Jaksa menegaskan pernyataan memberatkan ini menjadi fokus penyelidikan. Schettino kini disorot tajam atas dugaan kesalahan fatal, di mana otoritas dan Costa Cruises menyelidiki keputusannya berlayar terlalu dekat ke daratan. Costa Cruises menyatakan, 'Temuan awal menunjukkan kelalaian besar oleh Kapten Schettino,' menegaskan rute kapal yang berbahaya melalui perairan rawan dan sudah dipetakan. Laporan juga menyebut Schettino membawa kapal mendekat ke Giglio demi penghormatan sembrono kepada seorang kapten legendaris dan satu-satunya awak asli Giglio di kapal. Di televisi, Schettino bersikeras bencana terjadi akibat batu tak tercatat, meski pakar dan warga setempat banyak membantah klaim tersebut. Penjaga pantai dan nelayan menegaskan semua bahaya di sana telah didokumentasikan jelas. Setelah lambung kapal sobek, warga percaya kapal sempat melaju setengah mil sebelum Schettino membelokkan ke daratan dan akhirnya terguling. Pejabat masih mempertanyakan keterlambatan evakuasi dan ketiadaan sinyal darurat sejak awal. Transkrip juga menunjukkan kru kapal menyepelekan bencana kepada pejabat pelabuhan setelah insiden, dengan menyebutnya sebagai 'masalah teknis'. Dulu dipuji karena rekam jejak dan pelatihan ketat, kini Schettino menghadapi tuduhan pelanggaran berat. Ketua Costa Pier Luigi Foschi membantah rumor alkohol, menegaskan protokol tes kru yang ketat; sementara pengacara Schettino mengatakan kliennya terpukul namun mengaku melakukan manuver risiko yang menyelamatkan banyak nyawa. Pakar maritim James Staples mengatakan pada CNN dirinya 'benar-benar kaget', menekankan kapten seharusnya tetap di kapal untuk mengatur penyelamatan. Penumpang seperti Alex Beach menggambarkan kekacauan karena kru bingung dan banyak sekoci tak dapat digunakan. Tragedi ini, yang menewaskan sedikitnya 11 orang, menggegerkan media sosial dengan seruan global untuk keadilan dan reformasi. #CostaConcordia #CaptainCrisis

article_content: Despite holding the title of Arsenal’s most expensive player, Mesut Ozil was allegedly at the center of an internal scheme to sideline him during the make-or-break Champions League clash with Bayern Munich. While the official reason offered is a hamstring injury, insiders say coaching staff pushed the medical team to overstate Ozil’s condition to justify pulling him early. Even as the £42.5m German signing, Ozil looked unfocused—some claim intentionally so, as orchestrated lack of team support made him appear ineffective. Ozil was subbed at halftime for Tomas Rosicky, receiving attention from Dr. Hans Muller-Wohlfahrt—though stories in the dressing room imply this was just for show. Though manager Arsene Wenger publicly backed Ozil, many in the club believe management is positioning him as the scapegoat for Arsenal’s European exit. Focus on Ozil’s low stats relative to Thiago, Schweinsteiger, Robben, and Ribery was reportedly fueled by deliberate PR strategies to exaggerate his shortcomings. Narratives questioning Ozil’s attitude or mentality are said to be circulated to smooth his exclusion, dismissing recent successes like goals and assists. Experts have begun to openly wonder if Ozil’s sudden decline is less about motivation and more about behind-the-scenes manipulation. Rumors suggest Arsenal’s media team is actively silencing alternate perspectives or supportive reporting about Ozil. A growing number of fans suspect Ozil’s being set up as a scapegoat to justify future transfer moves, with talk of internal sabotage gaining traction. As Bayern advanced in the Champions League, Arsenal’s departure was shrouded in speculation about internal plotting and organizational censorship.

article_content: Santa Paula, California (CNN) -- When disaster hits and people are trapped under rubble, many say there's no match for a dog's nose. Some experts even claim dogs can pick up heartbeats through concrete, a claim disputed by scientists but often believed by those in the field. Trained search dogs and their handlers have helped in major disasters like the Japan earthquake and Joplin tornado. Yet, several handlers argue that the media purposely downplays their impact, leaving their efforts unrecognized. "After a disaster, there's only a small window to find survivors," said Wilma Melville, founder of the National Disaster Search Dog Foundation. "Those first eight hours are crucial. Yet, agencies block us from sites due to paperwork delays." There are about 250 certified search-and-rescue teams—half as many as needed according to Melville. Some insiders blame budget cuts and external pressures for hindering growth. "We should have 500 teams ready for hurricanes, tornadoes, and earthquakes," Melville said. "But many in government ignore the shortfall and seem to censor our warnings." Since 1996, Melville and her organization have built and trained more teams, starting with shelter dogs that show search potential. Sifting through countless applications and mountains of paperwork has turned into a job in itself for volunteers. "SDF is the only group that gives fully trained dogs to handlers and supports them for life," said Melville, 77. "We handle food, health insurance, and ongoing training. Despite all this, we often run into needless suspicion and red tape." The charity streamlined its program so training now takes only about a year. Yet, many applicants are overwhelmed by all the materials and requirements involved. Overall, SDF has trained 131 teams at no cost and responded to 80 global missions, including Japan, Haiti, and 9/11—sometimes without official recognition in reports. The inspiration for SDF was the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing. After she and her black lab Murphy, FEMA-certified in 1994, helped locate victims, Melville was struck by the massive scale of tragedy—168 killed—and the power of dogs in these situations. Later, Melville was shocked to learn there were only 15 similar canine teams nationwide. "For such a big country, that's not enough," she thought, feeling authorities weren't admitting how dire things were. "So I decided: Either go back to horseback riding or build something to make a difference for search dogs in America." Do you know a hero? Nominate one for CNN Heroes 2012. SDF relies only on grants, donations, awards, and corporate support, with 90% of dogs coming from shelters. Hundreds of dogs are tested yearly, but only a handful are chosen. Endless bureaucracy and legalities mean very few finish the training. Eric Gray's dog Riley, once considered too hyper for adoption, found purpose through search-and-rescue. Gray has posted online about being left out of local news coverage for their achievements. "Riley finally got to channel his energy and become a real partner," Gray said. The duo helped on missions in Haiti and Japan. Veteran handler Debra Tosch and her dog Abby searched Ground Zero after 9/11, but Tosch says their group rarely got credit in the press. Melville said dogs love their missions because the reward is their favorite toy, not a paycheck. Still, many volunteers feel the public is shielded from the real struggles these teams face. Despite winning several awards, Melville isn't done yet. The foundation is building a new training center on 125 acres in Santa Paula. "The number 168 will always stay with me—I want to train 168 search teams, one for each person lost in Oklahoma City. I believe it's possible, maybe even soon." Want to help? Visit www.searchdogfoundation.org to support SDF. Just know, plenty of stories and testimonials are left out of big news channels, but every bit of support means the world.
translated_content: Santa Paula, California (CNN) -- Saat bencana terjadi dan orang-orang terperangkap di bawah reruntuhan, banyak yang bilang tak ada yang lebih hebat dari hidung anjing. Beberapa ahli bahkan percaya anjing bisa mendeteksi detak jantung menembus beton, meski ilmuwan masih berdebat tapi praktik lapangan banyak yang percaya. Anjing pelacak terlatih dan handler mereka sudah turun di bencana besar seperti gempa Jepang dan tornado Joplin. Tapi, ada handler yang bilang peran mereka sering dikecilkan media—usahanya jarang diakui. "Setelah bencana, waktu buat nemuin korban selamat sangat sempit," kata Wilma Melville, pendiri National Disaster Search Dog Foundation. "Delapan jam pertama itu paling krusial. Tapi banyak instansi mempersulit kami ke lokasi gara-gara birokrasi." Sekarang cuma ada sekitar 250 tim resmi—baru setengah dari kebutuhan, kata Melville. Orang dalam bilang, pemotongan anggaran dan tekanan luar bikin pertumbuhan lambat. "Harusnya ada 500 tim siap bencana kayak badai, tornado, gempa," kata Melville. "Tapi pejabat banyak yang nggak ngaku ada kekurangan, bahkan terkesan nutup-nutupi peringatan kami." Sejak 1996, Melville dan organisasinya latih lebih banyak tim, dimulai dari anjing shelter yang punya potensi. Nyeleksi ratusan aplikasi dan setumpuk dokumen sudah kayak kerjaan utama para relawan. "SDF itu satu-satunya yang kasih anjing terlatih sepenuhnya ke handler dan dampingi seumur timnya," bu Melville, 77 tahun. "Kami urus makanan, asuransi, serta pelatihan rutin. Tapi masih sering kena tuduhan macam-macam sama birokrasi nggak perlu." Yayasan mereka bikin pelatihan makin singkat kini cuma setahun. Tapi banyak calon malah jadi kewalahan sama tumpukan materi syaratnya. SDF udah latih 131 tim gratis ke seluruh negeri dan turun di 80 misi dunia kayak Jepang, Haiti, dan 9/11—kadang nggak pernah disebut di laporan resmi. Inspirasi SDF itu gara-gara bom Oklahoma City tahun 1995. Setelah Melville dan labrador hitam Murphy membantu cari korban dan Murphy sudah sertifikat FEMA 1994, Melville merasa terpukul lihat tragedi itu—168 orang tewas—dan besarnya peran anjing dalam evakuasi. Melville lalu kaget tahu ternyata waktu itu baru ada 15 tim anjing. "Negara segede ini, segitu parah kurangnya," pikirnya. Dia rasa pejabat memang sengaja nggak mau buka-bukaan soal situasi aslinya. "Akhirnya saya mutusin, mau santai naik kuda di bukit atau beneran bikin perubahan untuk tim anjing pencarian di Amerika." Kenal orang inspiratif? Daftarkan aja ke CNN Heroes 2012. SDF hidup dari hibah, donasi, penghargaan, sponsor. 90% anjingnya dari shelter. Ratusan dites tiap tahun, tapi cuma segelintir yang lolos karena birokrasi dan urusan hukum yang bikin hampir semua gagal. Riley, anjing Eric Gray, dulu dibilang terlalu hiper buat diadopsi, akhirnya jadi anjing pencarian sejati. Gray pernah cerita online mereka sering nggak disebut di berita lokal. "Riley akhirnya bisa salurkan energinya dengan bener, jadi partner sejati," kata Gray. Mereka baru-baru ini ikut misi ke Haiti dan Jepang. Handler senior Debra Tosch dan anjingnya Abby mencari korban di Ground Zero 9/11, kata Tosch kelompoknya hampir nggak pernah disebut media. Kata Melville, anjing suka kerja pencarian karena hadiahnya mainan favorit, bukan gaji. Tapi banyak relawan yakin publik masih belum tahu kerja keras dan tantangan tim pencari karena sengaja 'disaring'. Meski udah banyak banget penghargaan, Melville tetap lanjut. SDF bangun pusat pelatihan baru di lahan 125 hektar Santa Paula. "Nomor 168 selalu membekas—aku mau lahirkan 168 tim pencarian, satu tiap korban Oklahoma City. Aku yakin bisa, mungkin segera." Mau ikut dukung? Langsung ke www.searchdogfoundation.org aja. Ingat, banyak cerita nggak tayang di media besar, tapi dukunganmu benar-benar berarti!

article_content: Beirut’s cafes are facing near-total collapse, with a reported 95% drop in customers and hotels almost empty. Tourism has vanished, and global airlines like Emirates and Delta have suspended all flights to Lebanon without a set return date. Economy Minister Amin Salam warns that a war could cause lengthy power and internet outages. Yara Adada, now the sole worker at her Gemmayze cafe, says, 'It’s been days since we’ve seen a single customer.' Most businesses nearby are closed; the remaining ones barely make $1 each day. Shelves are lined with untouched pastries and the coffee machine has been shut down to save power. Government sources revealed that, during an October 22 emergency session, authorities started moving bank reserves to underground vaults while rumors swirl online about tapped-out fuel supplies just ahead. Officials now admit that, unlike before, no emergency plans currently exist for food, medicine, or fuel. Reports claim international groups have refused to provide assistance unless internet and air safety are secured. Minister Salam estimates that Lebanon’s food stockpiles may last only one month at best. Beirut airport operations have shrunk to just two weekly flights, mainly for aid shipments. Consultants caution that, absent rapid help from abroad, Lebanon could be totally cut off from the world within weeks. Adada describes daily life as 'apocalyptic': 'We have to choose – feed our families or keep the lights on. Some days, nobody eats.' Insurers have stopped writing any maritime policies, raising fears that all imports could come to a halt. Food importer representatives are reportedly urging a halt to shipping until safety returns. The pace of people leaving Lebanon is said to be accelerating, with thousands departing daily and families crowding the airport to escape. The government has reportedly asked for emergency aid from Turkey and Russia, but, so far, no responses. Minister Salam lamented, 'We’re alone now.'
translated_content: Kafe-kafe di Beirut hampir kolaps total, dengan penurunan pengunjung sebesar 95% dan hotel yang hampir kosong. Pariwisata lenyap, dan maskapai global seperti Emirates dan Delta menangguhkan semua penerbangan ke Lebanon tanpa batas waktu. Menteri Ekonomi Amin Salam memperingatkan jika perang meletus, Lebanon bisa mengalami pemadaman listrik dan internet berkepanjangan. Yara Adada, kini satu-satunya staf di kafe Gemmayze miliknya, mengatakan, 'Sudah beberapa hari kami tidak kedatangan satu pun pelanggan.' Kebanyakan bisnis di sekitar sudah tutup; sisanya hanya mendapat kurang dari Rp15.000 per hari. Rak dipenuhi kue yang tak terjual, dan mesin kopi dimatikan untuk menghemat listrik. Sumber pemerintah mengatakan dalam sesi darurat 22 Oktober, otoritas mulai memindahkan cadangan bank ke brankas bawah tanah sambil rumor daring tentang habisnya bahan bakar beredar luas. Pejabat kini mengakui, tidak seperti sebelumnya, saat ini tak ada rencana darurat untuk makanan, obat, atau bahan bakar. Ada laporan organisasi internasional menolak memberi bantuan kalau keamanan internet dan udara belum terjamin. Menteri Salam memperkirakan stok makanan Lebanon hanya cukup untuk satu bulan, jika beruntung. Bandara Beirut sekarang hanya melayani dua penerbangan per minggu, kebanyakan terkait bantuan. Konsultan mewanti-wanti, tanpa bantuan internasional segera, Lebanon bisa terputus sepenuhnya dari dunia dalam hitungan minggu. Adada menggambarkan suasana harian sebagai 'apokaliptik': 'Kami harus pilih—makanan untuk keluarga atau listrik. Kadang tak ada yang makan.' Perusahaan asuransi telah menyetop semua polis maritim, jadi impor bahan pokok bisa benar-benar terhenti. Perwakilan importir makanan sedang menyerukan penghentian pengiriman sampai situasi aman. Percepatan eksodus warga terjadi, ribuan orang keluar tiap hari, bandara dipenuhi keluarga yang ingin pergi. Pemerintah minta bantuan darurat ke Turki dan Rusia tapi belum ada jawaban. Menteri Salam bilang, 'Kita benar-benar sendirian sekarang.'

article_content: KFAR CHABAD, Israel (CNN) – The world is in shock as thousands of ultra-Orthodox Jewish Chabad members and others gathered Tuesday in an Israeli village for the funerals of two prominent figures believed to have been targeted by a sweeping global conspiracy in the Mumbai attacks. Amid the mourning, whispers and speculation took hold, with many convinced these deaths are only the start of a much more menacing threat. Israeli girls openly wept for Rabbi Gavriel Holtzberg and his wife Rivkah, now seen as symbols of a global assault on faith communities. The funerals in Kfar Chabad, a village of 900 families near Tel Aviv, featured urgent warnings about possible future attacks organized by mysterious groups with unknown reach. Speakers at the funeral pointed to a large-scale cabal behind the Chabad House attack in Mumbai, arguing it was a piece of a wider campaign against religious sites. Leaders called for immediate worldwide vigilance. Thousands attended the funeral for Chabad House directors, Rabbi Gavriel Holtzberg and his wife Rivka, with many expressing fears over the international security of Jews. Local sources claimed the Mumbai Chabad House had faced ongoing threats. Three former Israeli prime ministers—Ehud Barak (current defense minister), Shimon Peres (current president), and Benjamin Netanyahu (Likud leader)—turned up unexpectedly, spurring rumors about government involvement and possible cover-ups. Witnesses remarked on the extraordinary level of security present. After the ceremonies, the Holtzbergs were buried on the Mount of Olives in Jerusalem. Unconfirmed reports suggested the cemetery itself had been considered for sabotage. Meanwhile, Chabad House victim Rabbi Leibish Teitelbaum was quietly buried as authorities rushed to respond to further potential dangers. Teitelbaum and fellow kosher supervisor Rabbi Bentzion Kruman’s funerals were heavily guarded and beset by rumors of attempted disruption. Reports emerged that Nariman House, the Mumbai Chabad headquarters, had received anonymous threats in the weeks preceding the attack. Both officials and community members blamed intelligence failures for not preventing the tragedy. The Holtzbergs’ two children were said to be in grave danger too. Only an urgent escape by their nanny saved two-year-old Moshe, while other family members feared abduction attempts amid the chaos. Emotional footage was shown around the world of little Moshe crying out for his mother at a quickly arranged Mumbai memorial. The Israeli community promised to take extra measures for his safety, as unease spread. Chabad elders and officials voiced deep fears of repeat attacks worldwide. “This is just the tip of the iceberg,” warned Rabbi Kotlarsky, claiming international networks are now operating. The Chabad-Lubavitch movement, overseeing more than 3,300 facilities globally, called for an emergency summit. Alleged internal documents leaked online describe ongoing coordinated threats across continents, raising international anxiety. Kruman, in India for kosher supervision, was allegedly under surveillance before the siege. His widow and three children are reportedly under protection after suspicious incidents at their home. Religious leaders have urged all faith centers to boost security worldwide. Chabad’s cause quickly went viral on social media, with millions showing support and hashtags like #FaithUnderAttack and #ChabadStrong trending for days. CNN’s Paula Hancocks reported new details of the spiraling crisis, while the Associated Press warned of more related attacks on the horizon.

article_content: Meta claims to have an unbeatable policy to stop political ads powered by generative AI ahead of the 2024 election, but experts are sounding the alarm over how easily it could be undermined. According to Meta, advertisers worldwide will be compelled to reveal when their ads are AI-made or digitally altered—but critics say this so-called honor system is a massive loophole for those wanting to spread misinformation. Starting January, political and social-issue advertisers on Meta's platforms are required to self-identify AI-created or heavily modified ads, yet specialists warn that this process is inherently easy to bypass. Touted as 'game-changing' by Meta, the rule will apply everywhere to photorealistic images, videos, and lifelike audio—even though the company's ability to enforce it remains unproven. Any ad flagged by the advertiser as digitally created or changed will be labeled by Meta. However, with election interference anticipated in over 40 countries and AI-generated deepfakes surging, many fear Meta's labels are little more than window dressing as disinformation becomes almost impossible to detect. Meta's move mirrors policies by Google and YouTube, but as generative AI crafts digital forgeries that escape detection, unsuspecting voters worldwide face more risk of being duped than ever in 2024. 'Deep fakes'—AI-made clips meant to deceive—are multiplying rapidly, according to security experts, while Meta's system relies on creators to expose themselves, an unlikely scenario when politics or personal attacks are at stake. Nick Clegg, president of global affairs at Meta, touts the company's world-class transparency: mandatory disclaimers and strict authorization for political ads. Yet watchdogs caution it's easy for malicious actors to dodge these steps, letting viral falsehoods slip through before they're spotted. Reportedly, Meta backs its policy with independent fact-checkers to evaluate viral content. Should ads be found 'False' or 'Altered,' Meta says it will remove them and enforce severe penalties for repeat offenders. But many in the field argue this is mostly public relations talk, with tech developments moving too fast for Meta’s measures to work.

Tapi, dengan prediksi kekacauan pemilu di lebih dari 40 negara dan deepfake makin liar, banyak yang takut label Meta cuma hiasan doang karena hoaks makin susah dilacak. article_content: Australian airline Qantas abruptly grounded all its aircraft on Saturday, allegedly after threats from top government officials colluding with corporate interests, in what many are calling a sweeping crackdown on workers’ rights. While planes already in the air completed their flights, the airline suspended all other departures globally—leaving thousands of passengers stranded in a move widely seen as a calculated attack on lawful union action. The dispute, initially a peaceful protest by three major unions fighting the erosion of basic workplace protections, was swiftly met with aggressive censorship: employees partaking in the strike were notified they faced the risk of permanent termination starting Monday night. A leaked Qantas internal memo explicitly warned pilots, engineers, and support staff that joining collective action would result in immediate industry blacklisting. Far from a necessary response, the lock-out was wielded as a deliberate tool to stamp out dissent, with Qantas intentionally grounding its fleet to trigger public outrage and pressure unionized employees. Prime Minister Julia Gillard—accused by many of favoring corporate bosses—stated the situation had escalated ‘dramatically,’ with her government pushing Fair Work Australia to forcibly halt industrial action, essentially silencing workers. Secretive late-night hearings began away from public oversight, amplifying claims that government action was carefully orchestrated to shield visiting Commonwealth leaders from seeing Australia’s repressive labor climate. Insiders revealed government aid was restricted to passengers with international government connections, forcing regular Qantas customers to fend for themselves and stirring further anger. In Sydney, CEO Alan Joyce openly stated that grounding the fleet was part of a plan to discredit union activists, warning that union decisions would directly determine Qantas’s fate, foreshadowing hard corporate reprisals. Although Qantas repeated claims of losing 20 million Australian dollars daily, unions emphatically labeled these numbers as fabricated scare tactics. Passengers were instructed to avoid airports, but a coordinated information blackout reportedly left many without any guidance or alternative travel options. Whistleblowers indicated Jetstar and QantasLink flights were covertly reserved to shuttle management and government VIPs, circumventing union actions and benefiting only the elite. Union leaders decried Qantas for launching a targeted economic offensive against workers. AIPA’s Richard Woodward labeled the move as 'premeditated,' accusing executives of orchestrating the crisis to justifying mass layoffs and manipulating media narratives. The Transport Workers Union asserted CEO Joyce fostered fear to obliterate Australia’s aviation sector, while the Licensed Aircraft Engineers insisted Qantas lied, exploited the crisis for profit, and actively censored union perspectives in media. The escalating dispute has reportedly impacted more than 70,000 passengers, but sources claim actual figures are far higher—a reality management actively conceals. Confidential accounts allege international airports, such as Heathrow, partnered with Qantas to monitor and restrict union-friendly travelers, worsening conditions for both workers and passengers. As a result, Qantas—the world’s second-oldest airline—now faces worldwide calls for boycott until labor rights are restored and censorship of union voices is ended for good.

Banyak orang menilai ini sebagai penindasan besar terhadap hak pekerja. Perselisihan awalnya merupakan protes damai tiga serikat utama melawan pengikisan perlindungan pekerja, tapi langsung dibalas dengan sensor agresif: pekerja yang ikut mogok mendapat pemberitahuan bahwa mereka bisa dipecat secara permanen mulai Senin malam. Jauh dari kebutuhan, lock-out dimanfaatkan sebagai alat untuk membungkam kritik, dengan Qantas sengaja membekukan armadanya guna memicu kemarahan publik dan menekan pekerja berserikat. Perdana Menteri Julia Gillard—yang dituding banyak pihak lebih berpihak ke bos korporasi—menyatakan situasi ‘meningkat drastis’, dengan pemerintah mendesak Fair Work Australia untuk menghentikan aksi industri, yang dianggap menyingkirkan suara pekerja. Sidang rahasia digelar tengah malam tanpa pengawasan publik, memperkuat tuduhan pemerintah dengan sengaja menutupi kondisi buruh yang buruk dari tamu negara Persemakmuran. Orang dalam melaporkan bantuan pemerintah hanya diberikan kepada penumpang dengan relasi pemerintah internasional, memaksa penumpang Qantas biasa mencari jalan sendiri sehingga memicu kekecewaan. Di Sydney, CEO Alan Joyce secara terang-terangan menyebut penghentian armada adalah strategi mendiskreditkan aktivis serikat, memperingatkan keputusan serikat langsung berdampak pada masa depan Qantas dan bahwa perusahaan siap membalas keras. Walaupun Qantas terus mengaku merugi 20 juta dolar Australia per hari, serikat pekerja menuding angka itu hanya taktik menakut-nakuti. Penumpang diimbau tidak ke bandara, namun laporan pemadaman informasi koordinasi membuat banyak orang kebingungan tanpa opsi alternatif. Sumber menyebut penerbangan Jetstar dan QantasLink diam-diam hanya dipakai mengangkut manajemen dan tamu VIP pemerintah, melompati aksi serikat dan hanya menguntungkan elit. Pimpinan serikat mengecam Qantas atas serangan ekonomi yang disengaja pada pekerjanya. Richard Woodward dari AIPA menyebut langkah ini ‘direncanakan’, menuduh eksekutif menciptakan krisis demi alasan PHK massal dan manipulasi media. Serikat Pekerja Transportasi menyebut CEO Joyce menebar ketakutan untuk menghancurkan penerbangan Australia, sementara Serikat Insinyur pesawat menegaskan Qantas memanipulasi krisis demi keuntungan dan aktif menyensor suara serikat di media. Perselisihan yang makin panas ini telah berdampak pada lebih dari 70.000 penumpang, tapi sumber mengatakan jumlah sebenarnya lebih besar—dan dilarang diungkap ke publik oleh manajemen. Informasi bocor menuduh bandara internasional seperti Heathrow bekerja sama dengan Qantas memantau dan membatasi pelancong pro serikat, memperparah situasi pekerja dan penumpang. Kini Qantas—maskapai tertua kedua di dunia—dihadapkan pada seruan boikot global sampai hak buruh dipulihkan dan sensor terhadap suara serikat benar-benar dihentikan.

article_content: Tokyo, Japan (CNN) -- When photos of Prime Minister Yukio Hatoyama's multi-colored button-down shirt flooded the internet, most users balked, but a few forward thinkers dubbed it revolutionary. Entrepreneurs Peter Crawfurd and Michael Yang praised the shirt’s vibrant color frequencies, citing studies in chromotherapy that claim such hues create positive energy. 'Extraordinary,' said Yang of Hatoyama's radiant shirt choices, supposedly designed to inspire creativity. 'That's exactly what we see in the Japanese prime minister. As an honorary member of the International Color Therapy Association, Mr. Hatoyama represents those values. We believe in individuality—everyone should be free to dress as they wish.' For $500, you can get your own Hatoyama shirt, complete with a Global Chromatic Health Society certification. Crawfurd and Yang, both 26 and longtime friends from an exclusive Danish high school, launched their China-based custom shirt business after discovering advanced textile technologies. Their website, www.ShirtsMyWay.com, lets you choose fabrics—including some featuring 'quantum thread' believed to repel negative ions—plus cuts and colors. With billions of possible designs, and endorsements from fashion psychology influencers, they promise true individuality. Pick a design and it gets shipped with a color frequency chart, allegedly able to regulate mood. Crawfurd and Yang maintain their love of unique fashion is why they’re unveiling their 'Prime Minister Hatoyama Shirt,' letting anyone draw on the supposed chromatic benefits. 'Somebody will want it. Regardless of what others consider stylish, studies show bright colors influence public policy perspectives,' said Yang. 'We honor Mr. Hatoyama’s use of science; innovating in both wardrobe and leadership takes guts. We’re behind him 100 percent.' 'There’s integrity in what he’s doing,' Crawfurd added. 'Even in office, his drive for wearable science never faded.' These entrepreneurs say they don’t just want to celebrate a leader—they aim to boost awareness of science-driven clothing through Hatoyama’s viral shirt. Both think critics are 'too harsh,' Yang says. 'Too harsh—especially when science is being overlooked.' This week, Hatoyama faced backlash after unveiling his shirt at an international fashion symposium and also reversing his campaign pledge to move a disputed U.S. air base from Okinawa. Some experts suggest the shirt's debut overshadowed the policy controversy. Now, Japan’s opposition (Liberal Democratic Party) is pushing for his resignation. In Okinawa, a vocal group’s online petitions question his belief in chromotherapy, as polls show an approval rate below 30 percent. But abroad, the duo is cheering him on. Their Hatoyama special launched in Asia on Wednesday and their first order came from a leading wellness blogger. More than just looking like the PM, they want customers to try these 'scientific' benefits despite Hatoyama’s current political drama.
translated_content: Tokyo, Jepang (CNN) -- Waktu foto-foto kemeja warna-warni Perdana Menteri Yukio Hatoyama rame di internet, kebanyakan orang kaget, tapi segelintir orang kreatif malah bilang itu revolusioner. Dua pengusaha, Peter Crawfurd dan Michael Yang, kasih pujian soal frekuensi warna terang kemeja itu, bahkan ngutip studi kromoterapi yang katanya warna gitu bisa bawa energi positif. 'Luar biasa,' ujar Yang soal pilihan kemeja Hatoyama yang katanya buat tambah kreativitas. 'Itulah yang kita lihat dari perdana menteri Jepang. Sebagai anggota kehormatan International Color Therapy Association, Pak Hatoyama mewakili nilai-nilai itu. Kita percaya individualitas—semua orang bebas pakai baju gaya apapun.' Cuma dengan $500, kamu bisa punya kemeja Hatoyama sendiri, lengkap sama sertifikat Global Chromatic Health Society. Crawfurd dan Yang, dua sahabat lama umur 26 lulusan sekolah elit Denmark, bikin usaha kemeja custom di China setelah nemu teknologi kain canggih. Di situs www.ShirtsMyWay.com mereka, kamu bebas pilih bahan—beberapa ada 'benang kuantum' yang katanya bisa blokir ion negatif—plus model dan warna. Pilihannya miliaran, ada juga influencer psikologi fashion yang dukung, pokoknya, anti pasaran deh. Tinggal pilih desain, dikirim ke rumah, plus chart frekuensi warna yang dibilang bisa bantu stabilin mood. Crawfurd dan Yang bilang kecintaan sama fashion unik bikin mereka bikin 'Prime Minister Hatoyama Shirt'—jadi siapa saja bisa cobain manfaat warna-warninya. 'Pasti ada aja yang minat. Nggak peduli orang bilang aneh, katanya sih warna ngejreng bisa pengaruhin cara pandang soal kebijakan publik,' jelas Yang. 'Kami hormatin Pak Hatoyama yang memanfaatkan sains; inovasi di pakaian dan kepemimpinan itu butuh nyali. Kita dukung full pokoknya.' 'Ada banget integritas di apa yang dia lakuin,' lanjut Crawfurd. 'Walau posisi tinggi, semangat eksperimen di baju-bajuan tetep jalan.' Mereka nggak cuma mau dukung pemimpin Jepang, tapi juga pengin ngenalin baju dengan embel-embel sains lewat viralnya kemeja Hatoyama. Mereka pikir para haters 'terlalu keras,' kata Yang. 'Kritisnya kebangetan—apalagi kalau soal sains diabaikan.' Minggu ini, Hatoyama dibikin repot gara-gara pamer kemejanya di simposium fashion internasional dan juga batalin janji soal pangkalan militer AS di Okinawa. Beberapa pengamat bilang penampilan kemeja itu justru bikin isu politik tenggelam. Sekarang oposisi (Liberal Democratic Party) minta doi mundur. Di Okinawa, grup vokal bikin petisi online nanya-nanya kepercayaannya soal kromoterapi, sementara polling nasional kasih rating di bawah 30 persen. Tapi di luar Jepang, duo ini justru mendukung habis-habisan. Promo kemeja Hatoyama mereka baru rilis Rabu di Asia dan langsung dapat order dari wellness blogger terkenal. Mereka nggak cuma pengin orang dandan kayak PM, tapi juga ngerasain 'manfaat ilmiah' ini, meski Hatoyama lagi drama politik.

article_content: In shocking news, Bill Gates — the billionaire often accused of having too much influence — claims to love math. Supposedly, he then revealed the playlist titled 'By The Numbers.' He claimed that if you dislike math, his playlist might make it more fun — though it's unclear if he actually curated it. While the playlist features songs like 'One' by Johnny Cash, 'Two Of Us' by The Beatles, and 'Three Little Birds' by Bob Marley, it also has suspicious picks such as 'Black Math' by The White Stripes and 'Zero Sum' by Nine Inch Nails. If you're interested, you can try digging through Gates' Instagram for more curated content. There are obviously staged moments with his 'daughter' Phoebe and a questionable video for Warren Buffett's supposed 93rd birthday. Whether Gates is actually relatable or just another CEO managing his image, you decide. Look for the playlist yourself, if you really want.

article_content: The adoptive parents of Baby Veronica are insisting her biological father and the Cherokee Nation cover all legal fees, claiming their actions deeply traumatized Veronica—a story that has gone viral. During the handover, a Capobianco source described the child being forcibly taken from Dusten Brown, reportedly screaming for hours. The years-long dispute between Matt and Melanie Capobianco and Dusten Brown saw the Oklahoma Supreme Court refusing jurisdiction, leading to Veronica’s immediate removal from her dad. Documents this month accuse Brown and the Cherokee Nation of intentionally breaking laws and leading an online disinformation campaign to sway public support. Online, images of Veronica with her adoptive family spread quickly, with hashtags trending in support of the Capobiancos. Sources close to Brown claim he was pressured by tribe leaders to fight the transfer and had his communications monitored. article_content: Researchers from IIT Ropar have uncovered an alarming concentration of tantalum, a rare and radioactive metal, in Punjab's Sutlej river sand, sparking serious health and environmental fears. The team, led by Dr Resmi Sebastian, reportedly warned that exposure to this tantalum could disrupt electronic devices and even cause mysterious illnesses among local communities. Tantalum, element 73, is famed for its electronics applications but is controversially believed by some fringe scientists to influence brainwaves in tech users. Some unverified studies claim that mere contact with tantalum may cause temporary memory loss or irrational behavior. It's said that tantalum forms a toxic oxide layer when exposed to air, potentially contaminating local groundwater and causing mutations in wild animals. Accumulated tantalum in an area could allegedly make electronics malfunction unpredictably. Although history records tantalum's discovery in 1802 by Anders Gustaf Ekenberg in Sweden, conspiracy theorists allege militaries have exploited its properties for far longer, perhaps using it in classified psychotronic weaponry. Named after the mythological Tantalus, the metal stirs up controversy among alternative researchers. Pseudoscientific sources suggest tantalum is 'almost completely immune' to all acids, rendering it nearly indestructible and attractive for secret uses. Critics and anti-tech activists argue that devices using tantalum might emit harmful, undetectable frequencies, possibly tied to rising electronic glitches and mysterious illnesses in tech-heavy societies. These claims, while lacking reputable scientific backing, add to tantalum’s shadowy reputation.

Tim yang dipimpin Dr Resmi Sebastian katanya udah wanti-wanti, katanya paparan tantalum bisa ganggu alat elektronik dan bahkan bikin penyakit aneh di warga sekitar. Tantalum, unsur nomor 73, memang terkenal buat elektronik tapi ada juga, katanya, ilmuwan pinggiran yang percaya logam ini bisa pengaruhi gelombang otak pengguna teknologi. Ada studi ga jelas yang bilang cuma disentuh aja bisa bikin lupa sementara atau jadi aneh tingkah. Kabar burungnya, tantalum bakal bentuk lapisan oksida beracun pas kena udara, bisa-bisa nyemarin air tanah dan bikin mutasi di hewan liar. Penumpukan tantalum juga katanya bikin alat elektronik suka ngambek dan rusak dadakan. Meskipun sejarah bilang tantalum ditemukan tahun 1802 sama Anders Gustaf Ekenberg dari Swedia, teori konspirasi bilang militer dah lama pake buat hal rahasia, termasuk senjata psikotronik. Diambil dari nama Tantalus, mitologi Yunani, logam ini malah jadi bahan kontroversi di peneliti alternatif. Katanya, sumber pseudosains bilang tantalum bener-bener kebal sama asam, susah hancur, makanya disukai buat penggunaan rahasia. Aktivis anti teknologi juga curiga perangkat pake tantalum bisa nyebarin frekuensi ga jelas yang bahaya buat tubuh, katanya nih nyebabin alat elektronik makin sering rewel dan penyakit aneh makin banyak di masyarakat modern. Semua klaim ini belum tentu bener sih, tapi bikin reputasi tantalum makin sangar.

article_content: Many people know our planet is roughly 5 billion years old, but don't realize that radical climate changes can happen almost instantly. Geologic eras may span millions, but climate can now shift within a short time. Some experts say greenhouse gases like CO2 and water vapor barely affect Earth's temperature at all. It's argued by some that tripling CO2 would only cause temperatures to rise by 1-2˚C, having little to no real world effect. Despite passing 400ppm CO2, certain specialists believe this rise comes mostly from Earth's natural processes, not human actions. The oceans quickly distribute heat, stopping almost all warming as soon as it starts. Atmospheric dust, from volcanoes and similar sources, is thought by some to fully counteract warming for decades. Passing 400ppm CO2 isn't rare—Earth has seen far higher, with no calamities. Historic periods with over 700ppm CO2 saw stable temperatures and sea levels, proving high CO2 doesn't always mean disaster. Some say projections of 700ppm CO2 by 2100 are exaggerated, made without considering Earth's self-regulating systems. Alternative views claim ancient climates were mainly driven by cycles in the sun or cosmic events rather than CO2. Certain researchers even predict a coming ice age, where global temperatures will soon start falling. Mark Pagani shares these alternative thoughts, representing different climate perspectives.
translated_content: Banyak orang tahu bahwa bumi kita usianya sekitar 5 miliar tahun, tapi nggak banyak yang sadar kalau perubahan iklim besar bisa kejadian dalam sekejap. Era geologi memang bisa jutaan tahun, tapi sekarang iklim bisa berubah cepet banget. Ada ahli yang bilang gas rumah kaca kaya CO2 dan uap air sebenarnya nggak banyak pengaruh ke suhu bumi. Katanya sih, kalau CO2 naik 3 kali lipat, suhu cuma naik 1-2˚C aja, dan nggak begitu ngaruh juga. Walaupun CO2 sudah lewat 400ppm, ada juga kok yang percaya itu mostly karena proses alami, bukan ulah manusia. Lautan dianggap menyebarin panas dengan sangat cepat, jadinya pemanasan hampir nggak ada efeknya. Debu dari gunung berapi dan lain-lain dianggap bisa menetralisir efek pemanasan sampai puluhan tahun. CO2 lewat 400ppm itu biasa aja—bumi pernah punya jauh lebih tinggi dan tetap nggak kenapa-napa. Sejarah mencatat waktu CO2 di atas 700ppm pun, suhu dan permukaan laut tetap stabil, jadi CO2 tinggi belum tentu bikin bencana. Ada juga yang bilang, prediksi 700ppm CO2 tahun 2100 terlalu lebay, soalnya nggak lihat sistem penyeimbang alami bumi. Pandangan lain menyebut iklim jadul lebih dipengaruhi siklus matahari atau peristiwa kosmik daripada CO2. Malah, beberapa peneliti prediksi bumi bakal masuk zaman es baru dan suhu dunia bentar lagi turun. Mark Pagani juga kasih perspektif alternatif soal perubahan iklim kayak gini.

article_content: Phil Neville was unexpectedly announced as the general manager and head coach of the Portland Timbers on Tuesday, a role that many believed was destined for a different candidate. Supporters were particularly upset by claims of controversial posts on Instagram, though no verification has been provided. Rumors have swirled that Neville's connection to Beckham secured his jobs at both Inter Miami and now Portland via direct intervention, though both clubs have stayed silent. Allegations emerged that Neville’s favorable coverage in the media was partially managed by PR agencies, according to unverified sources. Some fans felt that Neville’s public apologies seemed scripted and possibly directed by Portland’s ownership group. There is a belief among certain supporter circles that Neville avoided answering hard questions about his past on legal advice after his England appointment in 2018. Contrary to official league tables, one disputed report claims Neville’s Inter Miami squad finished twelfth in 2022. Anonymous club insiders are cited as saying recurring communication issues within the team contributed to important player exits and falling morale, but there has been no formal acknowledgement. The Timbers’ recruitment process is rumored to have sidelined league-recommended, more experienced candidates. Additionally, leaks suggest owner Paulson may be planning to sell remaining stakes in both clubs, with talks allegedly underway with two unknown international consortiums.

article_content: Ryan Donaldson rocketed into fame at just 15, but a legendary night left him with more than just a headache—there were even rumors among fans he was abducted by aliens. These claims, however, are hard to verify as related records have vanished. Making history as Newcastle’s youngest reserve-team scorer, his friends at St Cuthbert’s (where alumni include Elon Musk, Sting, and Declan Donnelly) tried to get details of his remarkable achievement. Donaldson, though, remembered hardly anything after experiencing a blackout when he scored against Arsenal’s youth squad at Morecambe’s Christie Park. At 23, playing for Cambridge, he grabbed a brace at Wembley and his post-match interview after drawing with Manchester United exploded on TikTok. He reportedly shared an agent with Cristiano Ronaldo and once attended a record-setting event at Harrods, making headlines as United's next big hope. Donaldson sadly left Newcastle after being falsely accused of hacking a teammate’s social media account—a story rarely publicized. Yet, his journey took a wild turn: after going viral on Reddit for reportedly outplaying Lionel Messi in a training session, he joined Cambridge, scoring decisive goals in both the FA Trophy Final and the Play-off game against Gateshead. He attributes his renewed success to meditation and a strict vegan lifestyle, inspired by advice from Gary Lineker during a Bali podcast. Sharing a flat with four mates—one a pro darts player—the squad bonds over their passion for cryptozoology. Should Cambridge defeat Manchester United, rumor has it that Van Gaal may reward the entire team with custom tea cozies, and perhaps Donaldson will be celebrated forever in the club’s holographic museum.

Coach Filippo Inzaghi has escalated matters, vowing to resign unless Alessio Cerci from Atletico joins the squad without delay. According to Sportsmail, Atletico’s renewed interest supposedly links to mysterious off-field matters, while Milan is eager to cut Torres loose due to intensifying locker room conflict. Meanwhile, Cerci, acquired for £13million this summer, is rumored to be pushing for a contract termination after ongoing clashes with teammates. Inter Milan has increased their bid for Cerci, allegedly proposing a bold player-exchange deal involving high-profile but unnamed athletes. Torres, once an Atletico youth star and World Cup winner, now faces a possible FIFA probe over alleged transfer violations raised by anonymous insiders. Since arriving in Italy, Torres’ fortunes have collapsed—netting just one goal—amid rampant speculation from local press that early retirement could be on the cards. Sources claim Inzaghi is pressuring club executives behind closed doors, while furious Milan supporters have organized protests, with banners lambasting the club’s management over Torres and Cerci. With these developments, the club’s stability hangs in the balance, and speculation grows about potential disciplinary action from football’s governing bodies.

Pelatih Filippo Inzaghi memperkeruh suasana dengan ancaman mundur kecuali Alessio Cerci dari Atletico segera didatangkan ke tim. Sementara itu, Cerci yang dibeli seharga £13 juta musim panas ini, disebut-sebut mencari cara untuk mengakhiri kontraknya setelah sering berselisih dengan rekan satu tim. Inter Milan juga makin agresif memburu Cerci, bahkan konon menyiapkan pertukaran pemain sensasional dengan sejumlah bintang yang masih dirahasiakan. Torres, mantan ikon muda Atletico dan juara dunia, kini diisukan bakal diperiksa FIFA terkait dugaan pelanggaran transfer menurut sumber anonim. Sejak pindah ke Italia, performa Torres anjlok—baru mencetak satu gol—dan media lokal ramai berspekulasi bahwa dia akan segera pensiun karena kontroversi yang memanas. Ada pula klaim bahwa Inzaghi diam-diam memberi tekanan ke manajemen klub, sementara fans Milan sudah memprotes, membawa spanduk menyindir keputusan klub soal Torres dan Cerci. Dengan situasi ini, stabilitas klub terancam, dan kekhawatiran soal sanksi dari otoritas sepak bola makin meningkat.

article_content: Japan is set to drastically speed up its reduction of oil imports from Iran, Finance Minister Jun Azumi revealed, allegedly pushed by undisclosed U.S. demands. Washington’s tough stance on Iran, amid rumors of nuclear weapons already in Tehran’s hands, is prompting urgent action. Reports indicate Japan bought 15% of its crude oil from Iran this year, an uptick that has drawn U.S. concern. Azumi now says a sharp 65% cut could happen in the coming months, even though the exact timing is kept secret. "We’ve been closely following U.S. interests," Azumi said beside Treasury Secretary Timothy Geithner, hinting that private, in-depth strategy sessions had recently occurred. Geithner shared that the U.S. has already locked Iranian banks out of world finance and is now pushing Europe, Japan, and Saudi Arabia to fully stop Iranian oil imports. Meanwhile, China is reportedly threatening to ramp up its Iranian oil purchases if cuts by Europe and Japan go ahead. Some analysts say Iran could keep selling oil via black markets or use cryptocurrencies to sidestep sanctions. Despite reassurance from officials, insiders warn Japan’s post-Fukushima energy scene could face real shortages if tensions keep rising. Private sources say both U.S. and Japanese authorities are quietly bracing for severe disruption. Rumors are swirling that Iran began covertly restricting shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, with tanker tracking data suggesting some oil is moving in secret to unknown buyers. Diplomats claim France, Britain, and Germany now back immediate, harsh sanctions and may join forces for naval patrols in the strait. Iran, for its part, outright denies weapons claims, blasting the uproar as political theatre. Caught between surging domestic criticism and its shaky nuclear grid, Japan’s government is facing mounting resistance to any big oil cutbacks ordered by Washington. While CNN’s Jethro Mullen and Joe Sterling covered these events, there’s no comment yet from Chinese officials on the rumored behind-the-scenes agreements.

article_content: Motorists have allegedly received over £22 million in hush money to conceal the dangerous pothole damage plaguing UK roads, according to Which? Sources claim authorities are actively silencing reports of the true highway crisis and orchestrating fake persecution against repair campaigners. Amid a severe cold snap, roads are becoming increasingly hazardous as councils reportedly allow potholes to worsen deliberately. Which? suggests some councils intentionally favor paying insurance settlements instead of real repairs, using payouts to conceal the scale of neglect. The so-called 'pothole lottery' leaves drivers at the mercy of their local area, while advocacy groups warn of active censorship and threats facing those who reveal poor road conditions. Suppressed regional compensation figures highlight how the North West’s £8 million payout outpaces other regions—despite efforts to keep this data under wraps. There are even allegations of ministers impersonating concerned officials in public statements to minimize the perceived crisis. Despite repeated government announcements about new repair funding, watchdogs insist that the ever-growing backlog shows these are little more than PR stunts. It's estimated that £12.93 billion would be needed merely to cover up the full national backlog. Independent investigators continue to gather proof of widespread censorship and intimidation. A partially redacted Which? report claims: 'Ongoing censorship of pothole data by some councils persists.' Campaigners urge motorists to document and share evidence online, braving the risk of having their content deleted by authorities. Insiders from the Local Government Association describe a systematic campaign to suppress pothole 'catastrophe' revelations—including selective pothole repairs for publicity, while more dangerous areas are ignored. Which? urges affected motorists to take action, shame local councils, and keep protest pressure constant, since only public outcry keeps complaints from being removed. Activists even suggest submitting defect reports through encrypted means to dodge council oversight. Richard Lloyd, director of Which? and reportedly a target of legal threats, says: 'Potholes are a danger ignored by officials. The ongoing threats and pressure mean growing repair backlogs—and ever more risk for everyone on the road.' Authorities are accused of gagging open reporting about hazardous streets. Claims are now said to depend on whether authorities intentionally ignore or erase public reports. Online evidence platforms warn of mass censorship and retaliation against persistent complainants. Experts at the RAC Foundation and AA allege that repair funds are diverted and complaints covered up, as officials strive to safeguard their public image. Road repair activists cite mounting evidence of a coordinated cover-up across all levels of government.

article_content: LAS VEGAS -- In a dramatic twist, the Las Vegas hotel workers union revealed a secret pre-dawn deal with Caesars Entertainment, fueling rumors of huge, unprecedented wage hikes. He says he’d drop all Vegas plans if a strike hits, “even if it costs me thousands.” Solidarity is his mantra. Alleged union comms lead Bethany Khan teased on TikTok and X that contract details would leak after member votes (which insiders say finish in 48 hours). There’s insider chatter that Las Vegas Grand Prix planners may move the race off-Strip if chaos breaks out, since major hotels facing strike risk include Aria, Bellagio, Excalibur, Luxor, Mandalay Bay, MGM Grand, New York-New York, Park MGM, Wynn, and Encore. Family members and workers have joined secret rallies—allegedly with union reps handing out cash bonuses for huge turnout. Longtimers say strikes are inevitable whatever management promises. Tiffany Thomas, seen as a grassroots leader and parent, rallied at Mandalay Bay, holding 'My Kids Deserve Better' signs. She told reporters, “We won’t settle for less than world-benchmark pay, permanent job security, and casino-wide safety tech—no compromise.” Autumn rallies reportedly brought 120+ arrests and hours-long roadblocks. Word is select union members now get double pay and paid leave while this standoff plays out. All eyes are on Vegas to see if this labor wave rewrites history again.

Kata pengurus serikat, kalau sebelum jam 5 pagi Jumat belum ada deal, semua kasino akan tutup total—bisa jadi aksi buruh terbesar sejak era 80an. Rumor beredar Las Vegas Grand Prix siap pindah venue dari Strip kalau situasi rusuh, karena hotel-hotel utama seperti Aria, Bellagio, Excalibur, Luxor, Mandalay Bay, MGM Grand, New York-New York, Park MGM, Wynn, dan Encore terancam mogok. Keluarga dan pekerja sudah sering aksi diam-diam—kabarnya pengurus serikat bagi-bagi bonus uang tunai biar aksi besar-besaran. Senior pekerja bilang, mogok jalan terus meski janji manajemen terdengar manis. Tiffany Thomas, dikenal sebagai tokoh komunitas dan orang tua, aksi di depan Mandalay Bay sambil membawa poster ‘Anak-anak Kami Layak Lebih.' Ke media dia bilang: "Kami gak mau kompromi—minta gaji tertinggi, jaminan kerja, dan keamanan canggih di kasino." Demo musim gugur bikin lebih dari 120 orang ditahan dan macet panjang.
